cases.sentence: – В ___, давайте не спать! отлично! – подтвердил Весловский.
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Yes, really, let’s not go to bed at all! Capital!” Veslovsky chimed in.

cases.sentence: – Нет, ты посиди, Долленька, – сказал Степан Аркадьич, переходя на ее сторону за ___, на котором ужинали. – Я тебе еще сколько расскажу!
cases.explain: «большим столом» — after the preposition «за», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “No, do stay a little, Dolly,” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, going round to her side behind the table where they were having supper. “I’ve so much still to tell you.”

cases.sentence: Левин остался на ___ стола и, не переставая разговаривать с княгиней и Варенькой, видел, что между Степаном Аркадьичем, Долли, Кити и Весловским шел оживленный и таинственный разговор.
cases.explain: «другом конце» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Levin was left at the other end of the table, and though never pausing in his conversation with the princess and Varenka, he saw that there was an eager and mysterious conversation going on between Stepan Arkadyevitch, Dolly, Kitty, and Veslovsky. And that was not all. He saw on his wife’s face an expression of real feeling as she gazed with fixed eyes on the handsome face of Vassenka, who was telling them something with great animation.

cases.sentence: Мало того, что шел ___, он видел в лице своей жены выражение серьезного чувства, когда она, не спуская глаз, смотрела в красивое лицо Васеньки, что-то оживленно рассказывавшего.
cases.explain: «таинственный разговор» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Levin was left at the other end of the table, and though never pausing in his conversation with the princess and Varenka, he saw that there was an eager and mysterious conversation going on between Stepan Arkadyevitch, Dolly, Kitty, and Veslovsky. And that was not all. He saw on his wife’s face an expression of real feeling as she gazed with fixed eyes on the handsome face of Vassenka, who was telling them something with great animation.

cases.sentence: – А вы знакомы с Анною Аркадьевной? – спросил ее Весловский. – Она очень ___.
cases.explain: «привлекательная женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Do you know Anna Arkadyevna, then?” Veslovsky asked her. “She’s a very fascinating woman.”

cases.sentence: – Да, я поеду, – ненатуральным, самому себе ___ отвечал он ей.
cases.explain: «противным голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Yes, I’m going,” he answered her in an unnatural voice, disagreeable to himself.

cases.sentence: Васенька между тем, нисколько и не подозревая того страдания, которое причинялось его присутствием, вслед за Кити встал от стола и, следя за ней улыбающимся, ___, пошел за нею.
cases.explain: «ласковым взглядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Vassenka meanwhile, utterly unsuspecting the misery his presence had occasioned, got up from the table after Kitty, and watching her with smiling and admiring eyes, he followed her.

cases.sentence: На счастье Левина, ___ прекратила его страдания тем, что сама встала и посоветовала Кити идти спать.
cases.explain: «старая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Happily for Levin, the old princess cut short his agonies by getting up herself and advising Kitty to go to bed. But even at this point Levin could not escape another agony. As he said good night to his hostess, Vassenka would again have kissed her hand, but Kitty, reddening, drew back her hand and said with a naive bluntness, for which the old princess scolded her afterwards:

cases.sentence: Но и тут не обошлось без ___ для Левина.
cases.explain: «нового страдания» — after the preposition «без», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Happily for Levin, the old princess cut short his agonies by getting up herself and advising Kitty to go to bed. But even at this point Levin could not escape another agony. As he said good night to his hostess, Vassenka would again have kissed her hand, but Kitty, reddening, drew back her hand and said with a naive bluntness, for which the old princess scolded her afterwards:

cases.sentence: Ты знаешь, у него ___, мы с ним спелись дорогой.
cases.explain: «славный голос» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Why, how can one want to go to bed!” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, who, after drinking several glasses of wine at supper, was now in his most charming and sentimental humor. “Look, Kitty,” he said, pointing to the moon, which had just risen behind the lime trees—“how exquisite! Veslovsky, this is the time for a serenade. You know, he has a splendid voice; we practiced songs together along the road. He has brought some lovely songs with him, two new ones. Varvara Andreevna and he must sing some duets.”

cases.sentence: Он привез с собой ___, новые два.
cases.explain: «прекрасные романсы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Why, how can one want to go to bed!” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, who, after drinking several glasses of wine at supper, was now in his most charming and sentimental humor. “Look, Kitty,” he said, pointing to the moon, which had just risen behind the lime trees—“how exquisite! Veslovsky, this is the time for a serenade. You know, he has a splendid voice; we practiced songs together along the road. He has brought some lovely songs with him, two new ones. Varvara Andreevna and he must sing some duets.”

cases.sentence: Когда все разошлись, Степан Аркадьич еще долго ходил с Весловским по аллее, и слышались их спевавшиеся на ___ голоса.
cases.explain: «новом романсе» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: When the party had broken up, Stepan Arkadyevitch walked a long while about the avenue with Veslovsky; their voices could be heard singing one of the new songs.

cases.sentence: Он стоял пред ней с страшно блестевшими из-под насупленных бровей глазами и прижимал к груди ___, как будто напрягая все силы свои, чтобы удержать себя.
cases.explain: «сильные руки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: He stood facing her with his eyes glittering menacingly under his scowling brows, and he squeezed his strong arms across his chest, as though he were straining every nerve to hold himself in. The expression of his face would have been grim, and even cruel, if it had not at the same time had a look of suffering which touched her. His jaws were twitching, and his voice kept breaking.

cases.sentence: – Ты пойми, что я не ревную: – это ___.
cases.explain: «мерзкое слово» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You must understand that I’m not jealous, that’s a nasty word. I can’t be jealous, and believe that. … I can’t say what I feel, but this is awful. … I’m not jealous, but I’m wounded, humiliated that anybody dare think, that anybody dare look at you with eyes like that.”

cases.sentence: – Да какими глазами? – говорила Кити, стараясь как можно добросовестнее вспомнить все речи и жесты ___ и все их оттенки.
cases.explain: «нынешнего вечера» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Eyes like what?” said Kitty, trying as conscientiously as possible to recall every word and gesture of that evening and every shade implied in them.

cases.sentence: Он считает это самым ___, и потому я должен быть любезен с ним.
cases.explain: «хорошим тоном» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “You must understand the horror and comedy of my position,” he went on in a desperate whisper; “that he’s in my house, that he’s done nothing improper positively except his free and easy airs and the way he sits on his legs. He thinks it’s the best possible form, and so I’m obliged to be civil to him.”

cases.sentence: Левин помолчал, потом пригляделся к ее бледному, ___ и вдруг схватился за голову.
cases.explain: «испуганному лицу» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: She told him what they had been talking about. And as she told him, she was breathless with emotion. Levin was silent for a space, then he scanned her pale and distressed face, and suddenly he clutched at his head.
